title: Reading Drill — Planning a route to a sports ground — A pilot study
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Planning a route to a sports ground — A pilot study
passages.body:
**A** A project in Brackenton began with reports of walkers leaving the official path near a sharp corner. The sports grounds officer had heard several complaints, but individual reports could not show how often the problem occurred. The team collected evidence using route observations and chose entries on informal paths as its main measure. That allowed it to compare different days using the same rule.

**B** The proposed response was an early directional sign. Rather than apply it immediately across the whole site, the team ran a trial in a single area. The trial lasted nine weeks. A second area kept its previous arrangements, making it possible to see whether any change occurred at both sites.

**C** The first review recorded the timing of matches as a factor that could affect the comparison. The team advised repeating the study under different conditions before drawing a wider conclusion. It kept the evidence from the first trial but published a note about why the figures might not apply elsewhere.
